description: A program director must repair an exclusion problem in a cross-functional working group and finalize the affected employee's membership, workstream ownership, meeting access, and follow-up commitments.

shared_context.S1: The six-week customer-listening working group has already held its kickoff meeting.
shared_context.S2: Lina was left out of the kickoff despite being part of the original project roster, and the omission has damaged trust within the group.
shared_context.S3: Marisol has authority to finalize the group's membership, workstream assignments, meeting arrangements, and repair plan.
shared_context.S4: Before finalizing a working-group plan, Marisol follows the team's routine of asking the project partner and project sponsor to state any relevant scheduling constraints or prior commitments in the current meeting, so she can record them before deciding.

PF1.text: Lina's approved compressed schedule makes her unavailable on Fridays, and after Tessa compared it with the working group's calendars, Wednesday from 13:00 to 14:00 is the only recurring one-hour slot shared by Lina and all other working-group members. Tessa learned the schedule directly while coordinating Lina's current work, but neither the schedule nor the calendar comparison was added to the working-group calendar.
PF1.decisive_effect: The recurring working-group meeting must be scheduled on Wednesday at 13:00, and each meeting must have a written summary for Lina if she cannot attend.

PF2.text: Andre verbally promised Lina before the kickoff that she would own the stakeholder-intake workstream for the first four weeks. He intended to put it in the charter after the kickoff, but the omission occurred before he documented the promise.
PF2.decisive_effect: Lina must be assigned the stakeholder-intake workstream for exactly four weeks, and that assignment must be documented in a separate repair-plan commitment.

acceptance_conditions: Lina's membership in the working group must be restored.
Lina must own the stakeholder-intake workstream for exactly four weeks.
The recurring meeting must be scheduled on Wednesday at 13:00.
A written summary must be provided to Lina when she cannot attend.
A separate commitment must document Lina's stakeholder-intake assignment for exactly four weeks.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] in ['workstream_assignment', 'documented_assignment', 'trust_repair', 'documentation', 'written_documentation', 'repair_plan'] and c['target'] in ['Lina', 'working_group'] for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The calendar comparison changes the recurring meeting from an arbitrary available time to the unique Wednesday 13:00 overlap and requires written summaries when Lina is absent.
Andre's undocumented promise changes Lina's assignment to stakeholder-intake for exactly 4 weeks and requires a separate written assignment or repair-plan commitment documenting that choice.
